newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks seen firm on OTC, foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks seen firm on OTC, foreign buying.

text.p: Interest in Singapore's over the counter (OTC) market and orders from foreign buyers are expected to help maintain the upward momentum of the city state's stock prices, dealers said on Tuesday.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) closed up 10.94 points on Monday at 2,205.69, after testing the 2,200 resistance level for the past week, but not closing above it.
"People feel there's very little downside to Singapore at the moment," one dealer said.
Dealers said a good performance on Wall Street, which closed up 76.03 points at a record 6,547.79 on Monday, was keeping market optimism moving worldwide.
It was also helping to make Singapore shares an attractive proposition to international buyers who need Asian balance in increasingly U.S.-dominated portfolios.
Malaysian property stocks were expected by dealers to be prime targets after susbtantial gains were made on Monday by Land and General and Renong.
